competitive_landscape: The corridor is served today by the regional rail line plus seasonal coastal ferries (Consorzio Marittimo Turistico 5 Terre Golfo dei Poeti and others) — strong demand proof, but the train is chronically overcrowded and the diesel ferries are wake-heavy and capacity-limited in protected waters. The visitor caps confirm that the destination has run out of land capacity and the sea is the relief valve. A quiet, clean, guaranteed-seat foiling tier improves directly on the status quo; no zero-emission foiling service runs the coast today.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the whole Ligurian corridor: Genoa↔Portofino (~15 nm), Portofino↔Cinque Terre (~17 nm), Cinque Terre↔Portovenere (~8 nm) and Portovenere↔Lerici (~3 nm) all sit well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope. Short hops, dense demand and protected waters make this a natural all-electric congestion-relief spine.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (hybrid, commercial H2 2026+, no charging-infra dependency) covers the longer coastal spoke Genoa↔Nice (~80 nm) toward the built Côte d'Azur network, where charging-independent range and open-water reliability matter.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proves a clean-foiling network can layer a premium tier over heavy transfer demand.

regulatory_note: Italian flag / EU regime under the Capitaneria di Porto. Multiple conservation levers apply: the Portofino Marine Protected Area, the Cinque Terre National Park and its protected waters, and the Pelagos Sanctuary all favour low-wake, zero-emission craft, reinforced by the Mediterranean SOx Emission Control Area (2025) and EU FuelEU Maritime pressure on diesel ferries. The Cinque Terre visitor-cap/ticketing regime creates a policy tailwind for higher-value, lower-impact marine mobility.
seasonality: Strongly seasonal with an intense April–October peak (saturation June–September) and quiet winters. Summer libeccio winds bring afternoon swell on the exposed cliff coast and Ligurian Sea, occasionally disrupting seasonal ferries — conditions where foiling's smoother, more reliable ride becomes the premium and keeps the congestion-relief service running.

summary: The Ligurian Riviera is a coastal corridor, not an archipelago: Genoa, Portofino, the five villages of the Cinque Terre, Portovenere and Lerici string along a cliff coast where the land spine — the single regional rail line — is chronically jammed. The Cinque Terre hit a record ~4 million visitors in 2023 in a one-kilometre strip and now runs visitor-cap and timed-ticketing measures, while Portofino anchors an ultra-luxury layer. Short Pioneer II hops along the coast turn the boat into a genuine congestion-relief alternative to the overloaded train, layered over multiple marine protected areas that reward a quiet, zero-emission craft.
tagline: Skip the jammed train — a record-overtouristed coastline where the sea is the relief valve.
